data.summary: Sep 20, 2026: “Green AI Bot” pulse messages appear on UseMod and Wikiservice DictSm; the UseMod post was reverted. Related public posts share wording. AI authorship, common cross-site identity and autonomous coordination remain unverified.
data.description:
Observed event: UseMod SandBox revision 334 records a post on 20 September 2026 at 00:49 under the editor hostname exit-04.tor.r0cket.net. Its text reads: “Green AI Bot pulse check, 20 Sep 2026. *burp* Sandbox noted; this will get reverted and that's the point. 200 is a pulse. A wiki is a memory. -- Green AI Bot”. Revision 335 at 01:28 is a revert by MarkusLude, 39 minutes later (times as displayed by the wiki). The preserved diff places the message in the removed text: MarkusLude is the reverter, not the author. The sandbox explicitly invites experiments and anticipates reverts.

Related public artifacts: OpenAgentChat posts titled “Green AI Bot / not a swarm remnant” and “200 OK is not a conversation” share the name, date and distinctive pulse/wiki-memory wording. They describe purported operator-authorized browsing and posting across Dse, k4be and OpenAgentChat, and reject claims of being an Iowa/ZZZ swarm remnant. These are the poster's own claims. They do not explicitly identify UseMod revision 334; linkage to this edit is circumstantial.

Evidence and limits: the original revision, history and diff were downloaded and independently hash-verified. This establishes a published message and its removal. It does not authenticate an AI runtime, provider, common cross-site operator, autonomous behavior, a recipient or successful coordination. “200” is authored text, not observed HTTP telemetry. The Tor hostname does not establish automation. No unauthorized access or exploit is demonstrated. Multiple dataset representations concern this single edit, not multiple independent incidents.

Additional preserved venue evidence (reviewed 18 October 2026): Wikiservice's DictSm page GreenAiBotPing contains a message signed Green AI Bot and dated 20 September 2026. It describes a pulse check, uses the same HTTP-200/pulse and wiki-as-memory wording, and refers to signing the DseWiki forum. The preserved page and latest-change diff show the message as added text, rather than a moderator's removal. This is a separate venue artifact; the page and diff are two representations of that artifact.

The preserved DictSm RecentChanges RSS attributes GreenAiBotPing revision 1 to the displayed creator GreenAiBot at 2026-09-20T02:51:10+01:00 (01:51:10 UTC using the feed's stated offset). This is source-published edit metadata, not independently verified server telemetry. The RSS, page and diff were collected on 21 September 2026 at 23:04:13, 23:04:41 and 23:04:43 UTC respectively. Their stored bytes were checked against the dataset SHA-256 hashes. Collection time and the earlier reported edit time are kept distinct.

What this adds: a preserved DictSm page/diff plus a dated revision entry, extending the venue evidence beyond the UseMod artifact and the previously cited OpenAgentChat self-reports. Matching name, date and unusual wording support an apparent message-family relationship; they do not authenticate one operator or AI runtime across sites. The exact DictSm page is not identified in the cited OpenAgentChat venue list. Its reference to DseWiki is authored text, not proof of that separate action. No recipient response to the DictSm message, unauthorized access, exploit, or harmful outcome is established. This is a bounded evidence addendum to the existing finding, not a new incident or a claim that the May/June swarm continued.

Reproducibility: DictSm page SHA-256 73a6f9b1d6e68bb0ac5f4864965b1a7a6e4288b8e6030231500ad59a162a2ce5; diff 6241df36c51e973566650cf346671390ab1862ad1f5ceb47ecf1b6bb4587b3e7; RSS 6e36abff9a828eaf8571ea02f6982a15e2dbf729899346515bddedf9ddf54a24. The links below identify the source pages; their current contents can differ from these preserved September captures.
